title: UNION ALL
description: UNION ALL is UNION without the deduplication step - every row from both sides is kept, even exact duplicates, which also makes it cheaper to run. Write a query that combines the `country` column of `customers` with itself using UNION ALL, so you get every country listed twice as often as a plain UNION would.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: UNION ALL

SELECT country FROM customers UNION SELECT country FROM customers would collapse right back down to the distinct countries, exactly as if you'd written DISTINCT once - UNION ALL keeps every row from both halves instead.
Select country from customers, put UNION ALL between the two queries, then select country from customers again.
expected_behavior: Returns the country column from customers twice over - twenty rows total, no deduplication.
solution: SELECT country FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT country FROM customers;
explanation: Reach for UNION ALL whenever you already know the two sides can't overlap, or duplicates are fine (or even expected) - skipping the dedup pass is real, measurable savings on large result sets.
